projects.title: Coorg — Destination Script Library
projects.description:
YASH XPLORE · Corporate life. Weekend escapes. Bangalore to anywhere.

This project is a reusable library: one script module per destination from your shared Coorg itinerary. Do not assign these places to a fixed day. On any trip day, open only the destination(s) you actually visit, record the on-camera part on location or from a safe parked position, and collect its matching B-roll. Record voice-over after the trip if needed. A visited place's script never implies you visited a different place.

Each module contains story-led Hinglish voice-over, flexible on-camera dialogue, a separate tagged shooting checklist, and source notes. Historical lines are based on Wikipedia where a dedicated page exists. Where Wikipedia had no dedicated article for the individual business/bridge/viewpoint, notes say so and no specific local history is invented. Raja's Tomb uses the official Kodagu district site because no dedicated Wikipedia article was found.

scenes.title: Dubare Elephant Camp
scenes.subtitle: Destination script · Use only if you actually visit this place. Not assigned to a particular day.
scenes.purpose: Wikipedia describes Dubare as a forest camp on the banks of the Kaveri in Kodagu. The article is brief, so do not invent a detailed founding history or promise elephant interactions.
scenes.notes:
HOW TO USE: This is one standalone destination module. It is not tied to Day 1, Day 2 or Day 3. Open it only if you visit this location. Use VO checklist shots for later narration and ON-CAMERA shots for spoken recording. Replace any conditional wording with what actually happened; never narrate a place or activity you skipped.

RESEARCH NOTES: Wikipedia describes Dubare as a forest camp on the banks of the Kaveri in Kodagu. The article is brief, so do not invent a detailed founding history or promise elephant interactions.

SOURCES:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubare
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kodagu_district

Wikipedia source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dubare. The article only identifies Dubare as a Kaveri-side forest camp; it does not support a detailed site history. Confirm current opening, river crossing/transport, and any elephant activity with the official operator before travel. Do not stage or imply animal contact.
scenes.voiceover: Coorg ke baare mein sochte hi elephants ki image aa sakti hai, aur Dubare ka naam isi wajah se itinerary mein aaya. Lekin main kisi jagah ko sirf ek photo-op ki tarah cover nahi karna chahta. Wikipedia Dubare ko Kaveri ke kinare ek forest camp batata hai—yahan river aur forest setting bhi story ka hissa hai. Agar aaj koi authorised elephant-related activity available hui, toh usko rules ke according hi record karunga. Aur agar activity available nahi hui, toh main us baat ko chhupaunga nahi. Travel story wahi honi chahiye jo actually experience hua, na ki jo hum pehle se imagine karke aaye the.
scenes.oncamera: Dubare ka plan banate waqt elephants sabse pehle dimaag mein aaye the. Lekin main yahan pehle current entry aur activity rules confirm karunga. Jo officially allowed hoga, wahi shoot karenge. Aur agar activity nahi hui, tab bhi river aur forest ke saath yeh stop apni ek alag story de sakta hai.

VO · Any official information or authorised activity actually available that day

scenes.oncamera: Yeh Abbey Falls hai, Madikeri ke paas. Ek interesting fact yeh hai ki Wikipedia ke according, falls ko pehle Jessi Falls kaha jaata tha. Yeh coffee aur spice plantations ke beech located hai, toh main waterfall ke saath surrounding greenery aur approach path bhi capture karunga.

scenes.subtitle: Destination script · Use only if you actually visit this place. Not assigned to a particular day.
scenes.purpose: Wikipedia says Madikeri Fort was first built by Mudduraja in the second half of the 17th century, later rebuilt in granite by Tipu Sultan, taken by Dodda Vira Rajendra in 1790 and had British additions in 1834.
scenes.notes:
HOW TO USE: This is one standalone destination module. It is not tied to Day 1, Day 2 or Day 3. Open it only if you visit this location. Use VO checklist shots for later narration and ON-CAMERA shots for spoken recording. Replace any conditional wording with what actually happened; never narrate a place or activity you skipped.

RESEARCH NOTES: Wikipedia says Madikeri Fort was first built by Mudduraja in the second half of the 17th century, later rebuilt in granite by Tipu Sultan, taken by Dodda Vira Rajendra in 1790 and had British additions in 1834.

SOURCES:
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madikeri_Fort
https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/History_of_Kodagu

Wikipedia source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Madikeri_Fort. Construction history includes Mudduraja in the second half of the 17th century, rebuilding under Tipu Sultan, control taken by Dodda Vira Rajendra in 1790, and British additions in 1834. Parts of the palace are in active government use; respect all closures and no-filming signs.
scenes.voiceover: Madikeri ko sirf misty hills aur coffee se describe karna easy hai, lekin is town ki ek political history bhi hai. Madikeri Fort ka first construction Wikipedia ke mutabik 17th century ke second half mein Mudduraja se associated hai. Baad mein Tipu Sultan ne fort ko granite mein rebuild kiya, aur 1790 mein Dodda Vira Rajendra ne control le liya. British period mein 1834 mein additional changes hue. Yaani yeh structure ek single ruler ki story nahi—Kodagu ki changing power history ka layered record hai.
